bibliographic.title: Generative psychometrics via AI-GENIE: Automatic item generation and validation with network-integrated evaluation
bibliographic.authors: Russell-Lasalandra, L. L.; Christensen, A. P.; Golino, H.
bibliographic.citation_apa: Russell-Lasalandra, L. L., Christensen, A. P., & Golino, H. (2026). Generative psychometrics via AI-GENIE: Automatic item generation and validation with network-integrated evaluation. Behavior Research Methods, 58, 217. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-026-03082-1

methodology.method_family: generative psychometrics; Monte Carlo simulation; network psychometrics; empirical scale validation
methodology.study_design: methodological framework (AI-GENIE) evaluated via Monte Carlo simulations across multiple LLMs and empirical testing with nationally representative U.S. samples
methodology.sample_description: five nationally representative U.S. samples for empirical testing; simulation conditions using LLM-generated item pools for Big Five personality traits and AI anxiety construct
methodology.sample_size: N = 4,964 total across five U.S. samples; 75 experimental simulation conditions with repeated text generation until 100 samples of at least 60 unique items per condition
methodology.sector: psychological measurement and academic psychometrics research
methodology.technology_context: LLM prompting for psychological assessment item generation, redundancy filtering, and structural validation using network psychometric techniques (EGA, embeddings); not a conversational AI or deployment-governance system

synthesis.main_claim: AI-GENIE can efficiently generate and select high-quality, non-redundant psychological assessment items using LLMs and network psychometrics, achieving structural validity comparable to traditional expert-developed measures.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces and evaluates a methodological pipeline combining LLM item generation with network psychometric filtering and validation across multiple models and empirical U.S. samples.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text does not discuss conversational system deployment, operational governance, auditability, compliance, or regulated-domain implementation; broader ethics and study limitations are not fully evidenced in the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central conversational-governance evidence. At most, it may serve as peripheral background on LLM use in research instrument development, not as evidence on governance of conversational LLM systems in regulated settings.
